Collaborators:
Less Wright
,
Howard Huang
,
Chien-Chin Huang
, Crusoe:
Martin Cala, Ethan Petersen
tl;dr: we used
torchft
and
torchtitan
to train a model in a real-world environment with extreme synthetic failure rates to prove reliability and correctness of fault tolerant training
Training loss across 1200 failures with no checkpoints.
NOTE: Each small spike is a non-participating worker recovering which affects the metrics but not the model
Introduction
We want to demonstrate torchft in worst case scenarios by running a training job with the most extreme failure rates possible.
Most LLM pre-training uses sharded models using FSDP. torchft supports sharded models using HSDP2, which combines a sharded model with the fault tolerant DDP all reduce from torchft. We’ve integrated torchft into torchtitan so you can use fault tolerance out of the box. torchft+titan also support other sharding/parallelisms within each replica group, such as tensor parallelism (TP), pipeline parallelism (PP) and more.
Here’s the structure of a training job with torchft:
The structure of the training job. torchft’s fault tolerant DDP implementation is used across the replica groups to synchronize the gradients. Standard FSDP2 and other parallelisms are used within each replica group.
torchft uses a global Lighthouse server and per replica group Managers to do the real time coordination of workers. The Lighthouse knows the state of all workers and which ones are healthy via heartbeats.
torchft implements a few different algorithms for fault tolerance. The two most primary ones are:
Fault Tolerant HSDP: An extension of FSDPv2 that uses a fault tolerant all-reduce. This exactly emulates standard HSDP training with per step all_reduce of the gradients and per step fault tolerance. This works best for large scale training with fast backend networks such as infiniband.
LocalSGD/DiLoCo: A fault tolerant implementation of semi-sync training. These algorithms minimize communication overhead by synchronizing at specified intervals instead of every step like HSDP. This is often used in communication limited training scenarios such as over ethernet/TCP or in geographically separate locations (federated learning or multidatacenter training).
We’re always keeping an eye out for new algorithms, such as our upcoming support for streaming DiLoCo. If you have a new use case you’d like to collaborate on, please reach out!
Cluster Setup
Crusoe
graciously lent us a cluster of 300 L40S GPUs. The GPUs were split up across 30 hosts, each with 10 NVIDIA L40S GPUs.
For the model, we used torchtitan with a Llama 3 model with 1B parameters to match the hardware available.
NVIDIA L40S GPUs are typically used for inference and thus gave us an opportunity to test torchft in a non-traditional environment where things such as DiLoCo really shine due to the lower TCP-only (no infiniband/nvlink) network bottleneck. The L40S has 48GB of VRAM (closer to consumer GPUs) so we used a smaller model and batch size. The average step time for training was ~9s each.
To maximize performance with the limited network, we trained the model in a 30x1x10 configuration. We had 30 replica groups (fault tolerant domains), each with 1 host and 10 gpus/workers. torchft can have many, many hosts in each replica group, but for this cluster, a single host/10 gpus per replica group had the best performance due to limited network bandwidth. We ran with 30 replica groups, as more groups stressed the coordination and reconfiguration algorithms more.
For network communication, we used NCCL for all communication (i.e., FSDP) within each replica group and Gloo for communication across replica groups. Gloo, while often not as performant, initializes much faster and can also fail much faster, which is important for quick detection of failures. torchft does support fault tolerance using NCCL for IB clusters with some caveats but wasn’t used in this demo. Since we wanted to maximize the total number of failures and recoveries, we used Gloo since it can reinitialize in <1s for our use case, and we were able to set the timeout on all operations at 5s.
For the fault tolerance algorithms, we did the bulk of the testing with Fault Tolerant HSDP, as it stresses the communication and quorum layers the most. For the final test, we used DiLoCo, which is a better fit for the ethernet based cluster.
Recovering with No Checkpoints
Traditional machine learning achieves “fault tolerance” by reloading from checkpoints when an error occurs. This involves a complete stop-the-world operation where all workers restart and load from the most recently persisted checkpoint.
With torchft, we instead focus on isolating failures to an individual group of GPUs. When an error occurs within that group we can restart that group asynchronously and all other groups can reconfigure and continue training without that group.
When that group recovers through a restart or the scheduler replaces the machines, those workers no longer have

data.title: A new pyramid-like shape always lands the same side up
data.author: robinhouston
data.article_summary: 数学家们发现并构建了一种特殊的四面体，这种形状总是会以同一面朝上稳定下来，证实了一个几十年来的猜想。传统的正四面体具有四个相同的三角形面，而这种新的四面体通过不均匀的重量分布，实现了单稳态特性，即无论怎样放置，它最终都会翻转到同一稳定的面。这一发现由布达佩斯科技经济大学的Gábor Domokos及其团队实现，他们成功制造出一个物理模型，验证了该理论。这种形状的制造需要极高的精度，其设计结合了轻质材料和重金属以实现精确的中心 of mass控制。这一成果解决了约翰·康威在1966年提出的一个未解问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一篇论文中提到的非均匀密度单稳四面体的讨论，及其物理实现和潜在应用。

不同观点：
• ColinWright提到自己与Bob Dawson在剑桥大学时曾一起建造过论文中描述的模型，并表示可能需要联系对方。这表明该模型曾经实际存在，但现在可能已经遗失。
• seniortaco认为这个物体不能被称为“形状”，因为其重心经过特殊处理，因此应称其为物体或刚体，强调重心分布对物体稳定性的影响。
• ErigmolCt感叹数学家John Conway提出想法，60年后有人真正实现了它，认为这是极具代表性的数学故事。
• kazinator指出该物体与Gömböc（一种均匀密度的单稳物体）不同，因为该物体的大部分质量集中于底板，强调其非均匀密度的特性。
• eggy对文章的前后发展做出评价，认为尽管早期看到视频时有些失望，但随着提到John Conway后，兴趣又回来了。
• ChuckMcM提出一个更复杂的构造问题，即如何构造一个具有不均匀重量分布的多面体，使其能够在两个面上平衡，且一个面比另一个面更稳定，并认为这种结构可作为防篡改检测器。

补充讨论：
• Elaris对物体的稳定性表示惊叹，认为它颠覆了传统平衡概念，强调平衡不仅仅是力的平衡，还涉及物体的内在特性。
• boznz开玩笑地建议将这种形状用于月球着陆器。
• tbeseda用幽默的方式提到了Vans挑战，试图将该讨论与流行文化联系起来。
• mosura对物体不能用均匀密度实现表示失望，并质疑为何不能通过打孔等方式实现。
• mannyv和WillPostForFood都提到这种形状可以用于星际着陆器，表明其潜在的实际应用价值。
• Retr0id希望看到一个标注重心位置的3D模型，以更好地理解该物体的结构。
• hashstring以幽默的方式结束了讨论，将该物体与日常生活中的事物联系起来。

争议焦点：主要集中在该物体是否应被称为“形状”以及其非均匀密度的必要性。部分讨论者如seniortaco和kazinator强调其重心分布对定义的影响，而mosura则对非均匀密度的实现方式表示失望。

A New Pyramid-Like Shape Always Lands the Same Side Up
By
Elise Cutts
June 25, 2025
A tetrahedron is the simplest Platonic solid. Mathematicians have now made one that’s stable only on one side, confirming a decades-old conjecture.
Comment
Save Article
Read Later
This shape can only rest on one of its four sides.
Gábor Domokos
Introduction
By
Elise Cutts
Contributing Writer
June 25, 2025
View PDF/Print Mode
engineering
geometry
mathematics
All topics
In 360 BCE, Plato envisioned the cosmos as an arrangement of five geometric shapes: flat-sided solids called polyhedra. These immediately became important objects of mathematical study. So it might be surprising that, millennia later, mysteries still surround even the simplest shape in Plato’s polyhedral universe: the tetrahedron, which has just four triangular faces.
One major open problem, for instance, asks how densely you can pack “regular” tetrahedra, which have identical faces. Another asks which kinds of tetrahedra can be sliced into pieces that can then be reassembled to form a cube.
The great mathematician
John Conway
was interested not only in how tetrahedra can be arranged or rearranged, but also in how they balance. In 1966, he and the mathematician Richard Guy asked whether it was possible to construct a tetrahedron made of a uniform material — with its weight evenly distributed — that can only sit on one of its faces. If you were to place such a “monostable” shape on any of its other faces, it would always flip to its stable side.
A few years later, the duo answered their own question, showing that this uniform monostable tetrahedron wasn’t possible. But what if you were allowed to distribute its weight unevenly?
At first, it might seem obvious that this should work. “After all, this is how roly-poly toys work: Just put a heavy weight in the bottom,” said
Dávid Papp
of North Carolina State University. But “this only works with shapes that are smooth or round or both.” When it comes to polyhedra, with their sharp edges and flat faces, it’s not clear how to design something that will always flip to the same side.
Gábor Domokos discovers and builds new shapes to understand the world around us.
Ákos Stiller
Conway, for his part, thought that such tetrahedra should exist, as some mathematicians recall him saying. But he ended up focusing on the balancing acts of higher-dimensional, uniformly weighted tetrahedra. If he ever wrote up a proof of his off-the-cuff 3D conjecture, he never published it.
And so for decades, mathematicians didn’t really think about the problem. Then along came
Gábor Domokos
, a mathematician at the Budapest University of Technology and Economics who had long been preoccupied with balancing problems. In 2006, he and one of his colleagues discovered a shape called the gömböc, which has the unusual property of being “mono-monostatic” — it balances on just two points (one stable, the other unstable, like the side of a coin), and no others. Try to balance it anywhere else, and it will roll over to stand on its stable point.
But like a roly-poly, the gömböc is round in places. Domokos wanted to know if a pointy polyhedron could have a similar property. And so Conway’s conjecture intrigued him. “How was it possible that there was an utterly simple statement about an utterly simple object, and yet the answer was far from immediate?” he said. “I knew that this was very likely a treasure.”
In 2023, Domokos — along with his graduate students Gergő Almádi and Krisztina Regős, and
Robert Dawson
of Saint Mary’s University in Canada — proved that it is indeed possible to distribute a tetrahedron’s weight so that it will sit on just one face. At least in theory.
But Almádi, Dawson and Domokos wanted to build the thing, a task that turned out to be far more challenging than they expected. Now, in a preprint posted online yesterday, they have presented the
first working physical model
of the shape. The tetrahedron, which weighs 120 grams and measures 50 centimeters along its longest side, is made of lightweight carbon fiber and dense tungsten carbide. To work, it had to be engineered to a level of precision within one-tenth of a gram and one-tenth of a millimeter. But the final construction always flip-flops onto one face, exactly as it should.

data.title: Save your disk, write files directly into RAM with /dev/shm
data.author: hiAndrewQuinn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用临时文件系统（tmpfs）或共享内存（/dev/shm）进行优化的利弊

不同观点：
• [支持使用tmpfs] @hackyhacky 认为可以通过将 /tmp 挂载为 tmpfs 文件系统，避免对 SSD 的磨损，并且一些 Linux 发行版默认就这么做。这种方法能使所有写入 /tmp 的程序都受益。
• [反对过度优化] @ctur 认为对小文件和普通使用场景而言，这种优化是不必要的。Linux 的缓存机制已经足够高效，使用 /dev/shm 可能会导致内存被遗忘的文件占用，并影响系统其他部分。除非对内存管理有深刻理解，否则使用 /dev/shm 可能弊大于利。
• [RAM 文件系统的长期使用经验] @1vuio0pswjnm7 分享了自己数十年来使用 RAM 作为文件系统的经验，特别是在编译时，磁盘速度太慢。他表示自己使用大容量内存来处理所有工作，并将长期数据存储在外部驱动器上。
• [Windows 上的 RAM 磁盘工具] @molticrystal 提供了 Windows 上使用 RAM 磁盘的工具推荐，如 ImDisk 和 GPURamDrive，并介绍了它们的功能和选项。
• [LVM 卷结合 RAM 缓存的设想] @Jhsto 提出了将 RAM 作为 LVM 卷前端缓存的想法，以应对高 IOPS 导致的 NVMe 过热问题，并询问其他可能的解决方案。
• [完全基于内存的工作流] @Waterluvian 反思是否真的需要频繁写入磁盘，尤其是在有充足内存的情况下。他提到自己使用 Git 进行版本控制，并且发现 64GB 内存足够支持日常工作，不需要频繁写入磁盘。
• [Jupyter Notebook 的使用] @slt2021 分享了使用 Jupyter Notebook 进行内存中状态保持的经验，提到可以通过 Notebook 记录和重现计算过程，并且可以在其中混合使用 Python 和 Bash 命令。

补充讨论：
• [历史经验] @ryoshu 回忆了在老旧硬件上使用 RAM 磁盘的经历。
• [潜在的命名冲突] @pizlonator 指出使用 /dev/shm 可能导致与 shm_open 调用发生命名冲突，尽管这种可能性不大。
• [简单直接的解决方案] @hacker_homie 建议直接将 tmpfs 挂载到频繁写入的目录。
• [简洁观点] @quotemstr 认为 /tmp 就是为此目的设计的，没必要搞复杂。

争议焦点：
• 是否需要对临时文件的存储进行额外优化，尤其是使用 tmpfs 或 /dev/shm。一方认为这是不必要的优化，另一方则认为可以减少对 SSD 的磨损并提高性能。
• 使用 /dev/shm 可能带来的内存管理问题和命名冲突风险。

data.title: Show HN: PRSS Site Creator – Create Blogs and Websites from Your Desktop
data.author: volted
data.article_summary: PRSS是一款快速、简单的桌面博客创作工具，提供友好的桌面界面和超越在线平台的速度。它支持本地AI（通过Ollama）和OpenAI（通过API密钥）的AI内容辅助功能。用户可以在浏览器中预览博客修改，并免费发布至GitHub Pages或选择自托管。PRSS提供便捷的入门体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PRSS Site Creator的使用体验、技术问题、命名争议以及平台限制

不同观点：
• **pidgeon_lover** 推荐了Frontmatter作为替代方案，适用于已经使用静态网站生成器（如Hugo）的用户，并指出其功能类似于PRSS，可以为SSG提供CMS功能。

• **yuppiepuppie** 尝试在Mac上下载PRSS后遇到文件缺失错误（ENOENT），并指出应用开发者在App Store上的名称显得不可信（含有随机数字和"Canada Inc."）。

• **jarofgreen** 对PRSS的运行机制提出疑问，询问其是自建的静态网站生成器还是基于现有工具，并关注其商业模式和定价策略，指出未看到明确的定价信息，但有鼓励用户联系支持团队的文本。

• **8mobile** 同样在Mac上遇到了与yuppiepuppie类似的错误，并寻求解决方法。

• **JimDabell** 对PRSS的命名表示困惑，认为其名称容易让人误以为是RSS的变种，而不是一个独立的网站创建工具品牌。

• **todotask2** 提到PRSS仅支持Mac平台，而他们的解决方案是跨平台的，暗示了PRSS在平台兼容性上的局限性。

补充讨论：
• 错误信息ENOENT在不同用户的Mac设备上重复出现，表明这可能是一个普遍的技术问题，需要开发者修复。
• 用户对PRSS的命名和品牌认知存在混淆，反映出品牌命名可能不够直观和明确。
• PRSS的商业模式和定价策略不明确，用户对此有疑问，表明开发者需要提供更清晰的说明。
• PRSS的平台限制（仅支持Mac）影响了其潜在用户群，特别是在其他平台（如Windows和Linux）用户中的推广。

data.title: “My Malformed Bones” – Harry Crews’s Counterlives
data.author: Caiero
data.article_summary: 这篇文章回顾了美国作家哈里·克鲁斯（Harry Crews）的生活和作品，重点分析了他的自传《A Childhood: The Biography of a Place》及其创作理念。克鲁斯在1941年经历了一场家庭暴力事件，这影响了他日后的写作。他常常探讨现实生活与想象生活的对立，认为通过虚构可以抵御现实的痛苦。克鲁斯的小说多描写底层人物的挣扎，尽管他的一些作品被批评为性别歧视或质量不佳，但《A Childhood》被视为描绘乔治亚州大萧条时期的杰作。他的作品融合了南方哥特风格与“ grit lit”亚 genre，展现了美国追梦者的复杂形象。

[Reviews]

by

An exhibition of Morrowâs photographs will be on view beginning in September at the Koger Center for the Arts at the University of South Carolina, in Columbia.
[Reviews]
âMy Malformed Bonesâ
Harry Crewsâs counterlives
by
Charlie Lee
,
Adjust
Share
O
ne night in early 1941, when Harry Crews was five years old, his father nearly killed his mother with a twelve-gauge shotgun. Looking back almost four decades later, Crews didnât find that fact particularly exceptional. This was Bacon County, Georgia, where in those days âit was not unusual for a man to shoot at his wife,â as he wrote in his memoir
A Childhood: The Biography of a Place.
âIt was only unusual if he hit her.â Crews and his older brother heard the shot, which blew the mantelshelf off the fireplace, from their shared bed. The shotâand the silence that followed. They fled on foot, mother and sons, down the dirt road to an uncleâs house, and the next day boarded a Greyhound bus to Jacksonville, Florida. In
A Childhood,
Crews recalls the details of their escape: the hurriedly packed straw suitcase, his fatherâs fury and frantic pleading, the sight of him frozen in the doorway under a kerosene lamp. And then, in the darkness of the road, a bizarre vision: âI began to feel myself as a slick, bloodless picture looking up from a page, dressed so that all my flaws whatsoever but particularly my malformed bones were cleverly hidden.â
Itâs an idea that Crews, the author
of fifteen novels and countless pieces of long-form journalism, often returned to: there is the life that is lived, and then its rival, a counterlife, where every flaw is hidden and one can feel whole. âThe only way to deal with the real world was to challenge it with one of your own making,â he writes in
A Childhood.
âFabrication became a way of lifeÂ . . . not only a way for us to understand the way we lived but also a defense against it.â What began as dissociation, a kind of trauma response, would become a program for art and life.
Crews was drawn to people who believed in self-creation, showmen who came from harsh places and thought that with a bit of artifice and money they could become someone newâon television, in politics, on the page. His own life seems to have been a series of guises or mismatched masks. âI have always slipped into and out of identities as easily as other people slip into and out of their clothes,â he admitted. Foremost among these identities was that of the âcrazy motherfucking freak from Georgia,â as one friend described Crewsâs calculated public image. He was also a college professor and inveterate brawler, a scrupulous journalist and legendary drunk, a Marine who boxed in his spare time and once wet his pants when punched. He admired James Baldwin and AndrÃ© Gide, claimed to read
Madame Bovary
at least once a year, and could recite Shakespeare at length; he bragged that he had never set foot in Texas without being arrested, and said heâd âlike to write a thing called
Jails I Have Known
.â Late in life he wore a Mohawk, had lines by E.Â E.Â Cummings tattooed down his biceps, and was described as looking like âa cross between G.Â Gordon Liddy and Vanilla Ice.â
Since Crewsâs death in 2012,
A
Childhood
has been widely recognized as a masterpiece, a Dickensian docu
ment of survival and blight in Depression-era Georgia. But the novels for which he was once notorious have found a narrower legacy: mocked when they arenât outright dismissed as the minor works of a windbag regionalist. Crews has become, alongside his contemporaries Larry Brown and Barry Hannah, an avatar for a gin-soaked, testosterone-fueled subgenre of latter-day Southern gothic known as Grit Lit. âFlannery OâConnor on steroidsâ is how the critic John Williams described Crewsâs work, not incorrectly.
Even his most passionate defenders must concede that many of Crewsâs novels have aged poorly, and a number of them werenât very good to begin with. He could lapse into the most
shopworn tendencies of Southern writing; the best of his books are marred by a dull misogyny. (Crews tends to
write two types of female characters: conniving nymphomaniacs and pathetic nymphomaniacs. Neither inspire his most artful descriptions.) But among the dross there gleam a few brilliant exceptionsâdeceptive, slippery books that defy the constraints of region and genre. They begin as pulpy entertainments but soon veer into murkier, more philosophical waters.
Many of the hustlers and fabulists who populate Crewsâs fiction are typical American strivers. âWe donât want to be bettern nobody,â explains a doomed guitar player in
The Gospel Singer,
Crewsâs 1968 debut.

data.title: Web Embeddable Common Lisp
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在浏览器中使用Lisp等语言进行WebAssembly（WASM）开发的可行性、进展和挑战。

不同观点：
• **jackdaniel** 提到正在进行改进浏览器集成和移植到WASI的工作，分享了一个被接受的资助提案链接。
• **deosjr** 分享了自己使用Sprtiely研究所的Hoot项目，该项目使用Guile Scheme编译成WASM，并提供了一个项目演示链接。
• **feeley** 提供了Gambit Scheme的相关资源，包括支持浏览器线程和JavaScript外部函数接口（JS FFI）的REPL，以及在浏览器中使用Emacs运行Gambit。
• **jinlisp** 提到自己正在实验WASI和GC扩展，并引用了四个月前关于Maxima（符号计算系统）是否可以在浏览器中实现的讨论。
• **bevr1337** 对LISP未能成为首批编译成WASM的语言表示好奇，并提到WASM项目使用表情符号跟踪项目进展。
• **tempodox** 幽默地回应了关于LISP在WASM中实现的问题，确认了CONS函数的存在。
• **b0a04gl** 认为浏览器字节码运行速度慢不是主要问题，重要的是在网页中实时执行和更新代码，Lisp可以通过WASM互操作直接驱动UI更新。
• **HexDecOctBin** 对WASM是否适合REPL驱动编程提出疑问，提到WASM的哈佛架构特性可能导致代码在运行时无法更新。
• **potholereseller** 提供了 fossil 仓库的源代码链接，但指出其最后更新于2025年1月。

补充讨论：
• **性能问题**：jinlisp 通过具体例子（如循环计数）比较了不同环境下的执行速度，指出在某些情况下速度远不及SBCL。
• **WASM互操作性**：b0a04gl 强调了WASM互操作的重要性，尤其是在共享内存级别，Lisp可以直接控制UI更新和状态变化。
• **项目进展**：deosjr 和 feeley 分享了各自的实际项目进展和演示，提供了具体的实例和教程链接。

争议焦点：
• LISP在WASM中的实现进展缓慢，特别是与其它语言相比，它的编译和运行时性能受到质疑。
• WASM是否适合作为REPL驱动编程的目标，主要围绕其架构特性和运行时代码更新能力展开讨论。

data.title: Build and Host AI-Powered Apps with Claude – No Deployment Needed
data.author: davidbarker
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一项新功能，允许开发者在Claude应用中构建、托管和分享由AI驱动的互动应用程序。开发者可以利用Claude的API创建这些应用，用户通过其Claude账户使用应用时，API消耗计入其订阅，而开发者无需支付费用。目前，用户已创建了AI游戏、学习工具、数据分析应用、写作助手和代理工作流等。开发者只需描述想创建的应用，Claude将自动生成代码，并可根据反馈进行调试和改进。技术细节如提示工程和错误处理由Claude管理，简化了开发和分享流程。该功能目前处于测试阶段，适用于Free、Pro和Max计划用户，但有不能进行外部API调用、无持久存储等限制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Anthropic新推出的工具及其功能、应用场景、潜在影响以及技术与商业模式的争议

不同观点：
• **技术乐观派**：[simonw]、[jonplackett]、[WXLCKNO]、[theptip]、[4b11b4]、[levocardia]认为该新工具功能强大，可以激发开发者创建各种AI应用，尤其是小型、定制化应用。他们强调了该工具的潜力和未来改进空间，比如支持外部API、持久化存储等。
  
• **商业模式质疑派**：[huevosabio]、[asdev]对Anthropic的商业模式提出质疑，认为依赖单一AI供应商会导致开发者被锁定，缺乏灵活性，并建议像OpenRouter这样的中立平台更适合提供这种服务。

• **SaaS挑战派**：[isoprophlex]、[bionhoward]认为这种新工具可能对传统SaaS模式构成挑战，使得个人开发者可以绕过SaaS工具，创建自己完全拥有的应用，从而降低对SaaS工具的依赖。

• **负面体验派**：[kashunstva]分享了对Anthropic客服的不满，提到无故被封禁且缺乏客户支持，对Anthropic的信任度极低。

补充讨论：
• **教育应用潜力**：[4b11b4]指出该工具在教育领域有潜力，可以帮助教师快速创建互动教学工具，尽管不是所有教育问题都能通过AI解决。

• **跨平台限制**：[asdev]指出该工具的跨平台使用受限，只有当开发者和用户都处于Claude生态系统时才能正常工作。

• **API调用需求**：[realty_geek]、[theptip]提到当前工具缺乏对外部API的访问能力，但这是未来许多应用场景（如游戏、生产力工具）的关键需求。

争议焦点：
• 该工具的跨平台兼容性和对外部API访问的限制是否会影响其广泛应用。
• Anthropic的商业模式是否会导致开发者被锁定以及其客服问题是否会影响用户信任。
• 该工具是否会对传统SaaS市场构成重大挑战。

44379673.article_content:
Product
Build and share AI-powered apps with Claude
Jun 25, 2025
●
2 min
read
Today, we’re introducing the ability to build, host, and share interactive AI-powered apps directly in the Claude app. Now developers can iterate faster on their AI apps without worrying about the complexity and cost of scaling for a growing audience.
Build and host Claude-powered apps
Here’s what we built: Claude can now create artifacts that interact with Claude through an API— turning these artifacts into AI-powered apps, where the economics actually work for sharing.
When someone uses your Claude-powered app:
They authenticate with their existing Claude account
Their API usage counts against
their
subscription, not yours
You pay nothing for their usage
No one needs to manage API keys
Claude writes real code that orchestrates complex AI functionality. You can see it, modify it, and share it freely.
Community ideas
Early users have already used interactive artifacts to build:
AI-powered games
with NPCs that remember conversations and adapt to player choices
Learning tools
that adjust to individual skill levels and provide personalized tutoring
Data analysis apps
where users upload CSVs and ask follow-up questions in natural language
Writing assistants
that help with everything from scripts to technical documentation
Agent workflows
that orchestrate multiple Claude calls for complex tasks
Getting started
Start building in the Claude app by enabling this new interactive capability. Simply describe what you want to create, and Claude will write the code for you.
As you work together, Claude can debug and improve its own code based on your feedback. Once your app is ready, you can share it instantly through a link—no deployment process needed. Claude takes care of the technical details like prompt engineering, error handling, and orchestration logic, allowing you to focus entirely on bringing your idea to life.
What you can do:
Use a Claude API within your artifacts
Process files and create rich UIs with React
See, fork, and customize any artifact
Current limitations:
No external API calls (yet)
No persistent storage
Limited to a text-based completion API
This capability is available in beta to Free, Pro, and Max plan users.

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种用于处理ASCII字符块的组合子库，特别适用于可视化数据。组合子是一种通过组合程序片段构建新片段的函数。文中以OCaml为例，展示了如何通过基本构造函数（如`of_string`、`fill`等）创建文本框，并利用组合子（如`beside`、`above`等）将它们水平或垂直堆叠。为确保组合框的尺寸兼容，较小的框会被填充空格。文章还展示了更高级的组合操作，如`hconcat`、`vconcat`和`grid`，并通过绘制Sierpinski三角形示例展示了组合子的强大应用。这种方法直观且灵活，适合调试和探索数据。

Box combinators
✏
2025-06-01
✂
2025-06-01
Text boxes
Examples
Sierpinski triangle
Spiral
Data table
Closing words
Appendix: the Box module
A combinator is a function which builds program fragments from program fragments.
In functional programming,
combinator libraries
refer to a design style that emphasizes bottom-up program construction.
Such libraries define a few core data types
and provide
constructors
—functions that create initial objects—and
combinators
—functions that build larger objects from smaller pieces.
Combinators enable the programmer to use intuitive visual and spatial reasoning
that’s vastly more powerful than linear language processing.
As a result, solving problems with combinators feels like playing with
lego
pieces.
This article describes a combinator library that deals with two-dimensional blocks of
ascii
characters.
I’ll use
OCaml
to demonstrate the idea
Functional languages are a perfect medium for combinator libraries.
,
but you won’t have trouble translating it to any modern language.
Box combinators are my go-to tool when I need to visualize data programmatically for debugging or exploration.
Text boxes
I stumbled on the idea of box combinators around 2012 while reading chapter 10 of
Programming in Scala
, 2nd edition.
The chapter demonstrates how to use Scala’s object-oriented features to build a module for rendering rectangular text boxes (the authors called them
elements
).
This section describes the underlying idea without the object-oriented fluff.
The primary type in our library is the
box
: a two-dimensional array of
ascii
characters
Single-byte characters aren’t a fundamental restriction;
we could also arrange Unicode glyphs in a grid.
.
A box has a
height
(the number of rows) and a
width
(the number of columns).
There are two primary ways to construct a box:
of_string
wraps a string into a unit-height grid
Handling multiline strings is an exercise for the reader.
and
fill
fills a box of specified dimensions with a character.
The
space
and
of_char
constructors are special cases of
fill
.
An
empty
box has zero dimensions and acts as a neutral element; combining it with other boxes has no effect.
⊕
Primitive box constructors.
+-------------+
of_string
"Hello, World!" = |Hello, World!|
+-------------+
+----+
|aaaa|
fill
'a' 3 4 = |aaaa|
|aaaa|
+----+
+--+
|  |
space
3 2 = |  |
|  |
+--+
+-+
of_char
'a' = |a|
+-+
empty
= ++
++
Things get interesting when we start combining the primitives.
We can compose two boxes in at least two ways:
by stacking them horizontally (placing the first box
beside
the second)
or vertically (placing the first box
above
the second).
⊕
Box combinators
beside
and
above
stack boxes horizontally and vertically.
+--+        +--+   +----+
|aa|        |bb|   |aabb|
|aa|
beside
|bb| = |aabb|
|aa|        |bb|   |aabb|
+--+        +--+   +----+
+--+
+--+         +--+   |aa|
|aa|         |bb|   |aa|
|aa|
above
|bb| = |aa|
|aa|         |bb|   |bb|
+--+         +--+   |bb|
|bb|
+--+
For the composite box to have well-defined height and width, the arguments must have compatible dimensions:
vertically stacked boxes must have the same width, and horizontally stacked boxes must have the same height.
We solve this issue by padding the smaller box with extra space:
we
widen
it for vertical composition
and
heighten
it for horizontal composition.
We can add the padding before, after, or around the smaller box.
Since none of the options is inherently superior, we provide all three, using central alignment as the default.
+---+   +-------+
widen
7 |aaa| = |  aaa  |
+---+   +-------+
+-+
+-+   | |
heighten
3 |b| = |b|
+-+   | |
+-+
+---+              +----+
|aaa|        +-+   |aaa |
|aaa|
beside
|b| = |aaab|
|aaa|        +-+   |aaa |
+---+              +----+
+---+         +-+   +---+
|aaa|
above
|b| = |aaa|
+---+         +-+   | b |
+---+
The
hconcat
(
concatenate horizontally
) and
vconcat
(
concatenate vertically
)
stack an array of boxes (
beside
and
above
compose exactly two boxes).
The
grid
function takes a
2-d
array of boxes,
combines each row horizontally,
and then combines the rows vertically.
⊕
Box combinators operating on arrays of boxes.
+-+  +-+  +-+      +---+
hconcat
[| |a|; |b|; |c| |] = |abc|
+-+  +-+  +-+      +---+
+-+
+-+  +-+  +-+      |a|
vconcat
[| |a|; |b|; |c| |] = |b|
+-+  +-+  +-+      |c|
+-+
+-+  +-+        +-+  +-+         +--+
grid
[| [| |a|; |b| |]; [| |c|; |d| |] |] = |ab|
+-+  +-+        +-+  +-+         |cd|
+--+
Examples
Sierpinski triangle
Box combinators are a powerful tool for playing with fractals.
Rendering a
Sierpinski triangle
requires only a few lines of code.
⊕
A program drawing a Sierpinski triangle of order
n
.
let rec
sierpinski n =
if n == 0 then Box.of_char '*'
else let s = sierpinski (n - 1) in
Box.above s (Box.hconcat [| s; Box.of_char ' '; s |])
⊕
A Sierpinski triangle rendered using box combinators.
$ sierpinski 5 |> Box.print_box

* * * *
*       *
* *     * *
*   *   *   *
* * * * * * * *
*               *

data.title: Nintendo Switch 2 Slammed for Poor Display–120 Hz with 30 FPS Response Times
data.author: kristianp
data.article_summary: 《Nintendo Switch 2显示效果遭批评：120 Hz屏幕响应时间为30 FPS》一文指出，尽管Nintendo Switch 2首四日销量突破350万台，但其显示性能未达预期。尽管官方宣称支持120 Hz刷新率，实际测试显示平均响应时间高达33毫秒，低于60 FPS的理想值，甚至不如原版Switch。亮度提升至约400尼特，但对比度和HDR表现不佳。推测原因可能是为了省电而未启用过驱技术。整体图像清晰度在较高分辨率下有所牺牲，可能通过固件更新解决。此外，单一面板背光也影响了HDR体验。用户和评论对其表现感到失望，认为可能为后续机型留出改进空间。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Nintendo Switch 2 的技术规格（特别是响应时间、帧率）以及其对消费者购买决策的影响

不同观点：
• [技术细节关注者 - davidhyde] 指出文章中关于60 FPS测试中响应时间计算的不准确，强调正确计算应为16.66毫秒，并解释如果超过这个时间，帧率可能下降到30 FPS。该评论关注技术细节的精确性。

• [价格与市场定位 - philosophyt] 认为如果Nintendo Switch 2价格便宜100美元且没有显示屏，可能会吸引更多消费者购买。该观点关注产品的市场定价和设计对销售的影响。

• [游戏内容优先 - tibbydudeza] 指出Nintendo的用户并不关心技术规格，他们更在意游戏内容本身。该评论认为Nintendo的用户群体主要关注游戏的可玩性和独占内容，而非硬件参数。

• [消费者群体分析 - neighbour] 认为关心显示响应时间的人群和购买Switch 2的人群重叠较少。大多数购买者是为了玩像Splatoon、Zelda、Mario和Animal Crossing这样的游戏，并且他们更重视便携性和游戏独特性。该评论进一步支持了tibbydudeza的观点，认为硬件参数对Nintendo用户影响较小。

• [年轻消费者群体 - v5v3] 认为Switch的主要用户群体是年轻人，他们不会太在意技术规格。

• [对技术讨论的批评 - zapzupnz] 批评文章评论区中的一些人过于关注技术规格，而不是实际游戏体验。同时指出关于屏幕保护膜和屏幕脆弱性等讨论是没有根据的愤怒。该评论认为，这些技术讨论脱离了实际使用场景，且对真正拥有或打算购买该产品的人影响不大。

• [技术规格与实际体验的关系 - UltraSane] 认为LCD显示器的刷新率应与其最大灰阶响应时间相匹配，超过该时间的响应时间被认为是“不诚实且愚蠢的”。该评论强调技术规格应与实际用户体验一致。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于技术规格（特别是响应时间）是否对消费者的购买决策产生重要影响。一部分人认为Nintendo用户更关注游戏内容和便携性，而非硬件参数；另一部分人则对技术细节和规格准确性表现出强烈的关注。

• 讨论中还涉及到对文章及评论区中不合理批评的反驳，如zapzupnz指出许多评论者并不拥有产品，且他们的愤怒是没有根据的。

• 总体而言，讨论反映了不同消费者群体对技术参数和实际体验的不同重视程度。

44391600.article_content:
Thursday, June 26th 2025
Nintendo Switch 2 Slammed for Poor Display—120 Hz With 30 FPS Response Times
by
Cpt.Jank
Yesterday, 02:02
Discuss (59 Comments)
Despite the Nintendo Switch 2 offering rather modest specifications by today's standards, even for a handheld gaming device, it has already broken console sales records with
over 3.5 million sales
in its first four days on the market. The on-paper specs claim that the Nintendo Switch 2 is capable of 120 Hz, promising a sizeable upgrade over the 60 FPS display of the original Switch and Switch OLED. Recent testing by
Monitors Unboxed
and
Digital Foundry
, however, reveal that these claims may be less than honest, since the handheld console's real-world performance falls short by a fair margin.
The most noticeable issue with the Nintendo Switch 2's display is the response times. Despite having a 120 Hz display, Monitors Unboxed found in its testing that the display achieved an average response time of as high as 33 ms. While testing was conducted at 60 FPS, the response times even fall short of this low bar, with 16.67 ms being the slowest response time required for the pixels to refresh between frames such as to avoid blur or smearing. Even the original Nintendo Switch manages faster response times, with an average of 21.3 ms. This is further exemplified by the Blur Busters test conducted by Monitors Unboxed, where significant loss of detail can be seen in fast-moving objects. Brightness was better on the Switch 2 in Monitors Unboxed's testing, measuring in at around 400 nits, but contrast is less than spectacular, with contrast ratios measuring in at just 1068:1. Color performance was also good on the new Switch 2, with 97.6% coverage of the DCI-P3 color gamut, however HDR performance suffered from the relatively low brightness and a lack of color management, which makes Switch 1 games seem more saturated than intended.
Monitors Unboxed goes on to theorize that the Switch 2's display is slow because Nintendo has seemingly not enabled overdrive and may be running additional low-voltage settings, likely to conserve energy and extend battery life. The end result of this is that, while the Nintendo Switch 2 may feel more responsive to play on, especially at 120 FPS, it comes at a noticeable sacrifice in image clarity at those higher resolutions. The likely cause of these slow response times also means Nintendo could theoretically address the issues with a firmware update.
Digital Foundry found similar results in its testing, with the publication similarly criticizing the Switch 2's display for its poor motion performance but also adding that the Switch 2's backlight is disappointingly a single panel instead of using dimming zones or something like a mini LED display, making a "true HDR" experience impossible on the Switch 2's built-in display.

data.title: Hurricane forecasters scrambling after sudden shutdown of key satellites
data.author: anigbrowl
data.article_summary: 美国国防部突然宣布关闭关键卫星项目，严重影响飓风预报。这些卫星属于国防气象卫星计划，提供实时图像和数据，对监测夜间风暴尤为重要。前国家飓风中心主任詹姆斯·富兰克林表示，此举将导致飓风中心识别风暴增强的延迟，特别是快速增强的预报将受到影响。正值预计大西洋飓风季活动高于正常水平之际，这一决定令气象学家感到意外和担忧。前NOAA官员称从未见过类似情况，对飓风预报工作造成显著冲击。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DMSP卫星项目终止对飓风预报的影响以及替代方案的有效性。

不同观点：
• 观点一：BenjiWiebe认为，DMSP项目的终止是可以理解的，因为国会已经在2015年投票终止该项目，且最后一颗DMSP卫星发射失败。他认为项目接近生命周期末期，逐步淘汰是合理的。

ZigJR - JSON-RPC 2.0 Library for Zig
ZigJR is a lightweight Zig library providing a full implementation of the JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol,
with message streaming on top, and a smart function dispatcher that turns native Zig functions
into RPC handlers. It aims to make building JSON-RPC applications in Zig simple and straightforward.
This small library is packed with the following features:
Parsing and composing JSON-RPC 2.0 messages.
Support for Request, Response, Notification, and Error JSON-RPC 2.0 messages.
Support for batch requests and batch responses in JSON-RPC 2.0.
Message streaming via delimiter based streams (
\n
, etc.).
Message streaming via
Content-Length
header-based streams.
RPC pipeline to process the full request-to-response lifecycle.
Native Zig functions as message handlers with automatic type mapping.
Flexible logging mechanism for inspecting the JSON-RPC messages.

data.title: E.A. Spitzka's Studies of Exceptional and Deviant Brains (2024)
data.author: Hooke
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了美国神经解剖学家Edward Anthony Spitzka（1876–1922）的生平及其对异常大脑的研究。Spitzka因对刺杀总统William McKinley的凶手Leon Czolgosz进行尸检而闻名，他试图通过研究极端个体的大脑结构来理解异常行为和天才的生理基础。他的研究对象包括著名地质学家John Wesley Powell、行为怪异的商人George Francis Train以及诗人Walt Whitman。此外，Spitzka还研究了多位死刑犯的大脑，包括谋杀孕妇的Chester Gillette和杀害船长的Frank Henry Burness等，探索犯罪行为的生物学根源。The Huntington图书馆收藏了Spitzka的大量个人和专业文件，为神经科学和美国历史的研究提供了宝贵资料。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Spitzka研究成果及其意义的评价

不同观点：
• vonnik的观点：对Spitzka能够承认自己多年研究走进了死胡同表示赞赏。vonnik认为，尽管Spitzka进行了广泛的研究，但他在解释犯罪行为或天才的复杂性方面没有找到决定性的证据。这表明vonnik认可Spitzka自我反思和质疑已有信念的科学精神。

• 隐含的另一种观点：可能存在对Spitzka工作的不同评价。一些人可能认为Spitzka的研究失败了，因为没有得出明确结论；而vonnik则从积极的角度看待，认为Spitzka对原有观点的怀疑和挑战具有科学价值。

补充讨论：
• Spitzka的研究质疑了当时流行的将人类行为简单归因于大脑结构和形态的还原论观点。这表明在科学探索中，敢于质疑和推翻现有理论也是推动知识进步的重要部分。
• 争议的焦点可能在于：Spitzka的研究是否真的走进了死胡同，还是他的研究为后续科学探索奠定了基础，只是当时未被充分理解或认可。

The Huntington’s blog takes you behind the scenes for a scholarly view of the collections.
E.A. Spitzka’s Studies of Exceptional and Deviant Brains
Posted on
Tue., Dec. 3, 2024
by
Joel A.
Klein, Ph.D.
Previous slide
Next slide
Edward Anthony Spitzka, from
Empire State Notables, 1914
(New York: Hartwell Stafford, 1914).
| Library of Congress.
Edward Anthony Spitzka (1876–1922) was a fourth-year medical student at Columbia University when he gained national attention for performing the autopsy of Leon Czolgosz, the man executed for assassinating President William McKinley. Spitzka, an emerging figure in neuroanatomy and brain morphology, was undoubtedly selected for this prominent task due to his father, Edward Charles Spitzka, who had testified on the insanity of Charles Guiteau, President James Garfield’s assassin, nearly a quarter-century earlier.
Previous slide
Next slide
1
of
3
Mugshots of Leon Czolgosz, ca. September 1901, after he shot President McKinley.
| The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens.
E.A. Spitzka’s postmortem drawing of Czolgosz’s brain, Oct. 29, 1901. Spitzka’s examination of Czolgosz’s brain revealed no major abnormalities and provided no indication that he was insane at the time of the assassination.
| The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens.
Newspaper clipping illustrating Czolgosz’s final moments. Edward Anthony Spitzka and Edward Charles Spitzka papers.
| The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens.
The younger Spitzka’s career flourished after he took a position at Thomas Jefferson University in Philadelphia, where he gained recognition for his studies on the relationship between brain structures and behavior. His particular interest lay in the extremes of human nature—both pathological and extraordinary—and he sought to understand the physiology behind deviance and brilliance. In addition to his academic pursuits, Spitzka served as the editor of the 1910 edition of
Gray’s Anatomy
, one of the most authoritative medical texts of the time.
The Huntington is fortunate to hold a substantial collection of the Spitzkas’ personal and professional papers, which provide a window into a transformative period in neuroscience, psychology, and American history. Before The Huntington’s acquisition, the collection remained largely unexplored, but ongoing research is beginning to shed light on its significance and much remains to be discovered.
E.A. Spitzka’s fascination with the brain led him to conduct postmortem examinations on several notable individuals, including Major John Wesley Powell, the renowned geologist, soldier, and explorer best known for his leadership of the United States Geological Survey.
Left: C.C. Pierce,
Major John Wesley Powell
. Right: E.A. Spitzka’s pencil drawing of Powell’s brain.
| The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens.
Spitzka was also intrigued by the brain of George Francis Train, a wealthy American businessman famous for his eccentric behavior and grandiose claims, including his assertion that he had inspired Jules Verne’s
Around the World in Eighty Days
and his declaration that he was the “dictator of the United States.” Spitzka even had the opportunity to study the brain of the poet Walt Whitman, though no formal analysis was produced after the specimen was accidentally dropped in the lab and shattered.
E.A. Spitzka’s tracing of a drawing of George Francis Train’s brain superimposed on Spitzka’s sketch of Train’s profile, made during an autopsy.
| The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens.
The collection also documents Spitzka’s numerous visits to Northeastern prisons to attend executions and perform postmortem examinations on murderers, as he sought to uncover the biological roots of criminality. Among the most famous cases is that of Chester Gillette, who was convicted of murdering his pregnant girlfriend, Grace Brown, in 1906 by striking her with a tennis racket and leaving her to drown in Big Moose Lake in upstate New York. His sensational trial became the basis for Theodore Dreiser’s novel
An American Tragedy
.
Spitzka’s postmortem study of Chester Gillette’s brain drew widespread public attention, as evidenced by this full-page spread from a 1908 edition of the tabloid the American Examiner, which catered primarily to British expatriates in the United States.
| The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens.
Other significant cases in the collection include that of Frank Henry Burness, who murdered ship captain George Townsend in 1903 over a pay dispute and later confessed to killing at least nine other people.
Left: Clipping from the New York Herald about Frank Henry Burness’ execution. Right: An information card from Burness’ execution.
| The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens.

补充讨论：
• Spitzka的研究质疑了当时流行的将人类行为简单归因于大脑结构和形态的还原论观点。这表明在科学探索中，敢于质疑和推翻现有理论也是推动知识进步的重要部分。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对某工具或平台的广告体验及其功能与安全性比较

不同观点：
• **jenoer的观点**：  
  - 对该工具的广告体验非常不满，尤其是无法关闭且重新弹出的广告，认为这是无法接受的。  
  - 更倾向于使用Cyberchef，原因在于Cyberchef是开源的，能够在本地运行（浏览器客户端侧），并且支持大量编码、解码和哈希选项。  
  - 强调了工具的安全性和透明度，认为开源和本地运行是Cyberchef的优势。

• **als0的观点**：  
  - 讨论了该工具的加密功能，指出其中只有AES是真正的加密算法，其他都不是。  
  - 对工具的加密能力提出质疑，暗示用户在选择工具时应注意其加密算法的有效性和安全性。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：  
  - **广告问题**：jenoer对广告体验的强烈不满，表明用户对工具的广告策略有较大意见，可能会影响用户的使用选择。  
  - **加密算法的有效性**：als0指出工具中只有AES是真正的加密算法，暗示其他选项可能不具备相同的加密强度，这可能误导用户选择不安全的选项。

• **工具功能比较**：  
  - jenoer对比了Cyberchef和该工具的功能，强调Cyberchef的开放性、本地运行和多功能性是其主要优势。  
  - als0则专注于工具的加密功能，特别是AES的唯一性，指出了功能上的局限性。

总体来看，讨论涉及了广告体验、工具功能和安全性等多个方面，用户在这些方面有不同的关注点和意见。

data.title: Is Lovable getting monetization wrong?
data.author: FinnLobsien
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lovable及类似LLM驱动软件工具的潜力和局限

不同观点：
• Workaccount2认为LLM工具（如Lovable）能够有效解决传统软件功能臃肿、学习曲线陡峭的问题。通过LLM，非技术用户可以根据具体需求定制简单工具，避免购买昂贵的综合软件包。他以自己使用Gemini创建CAD文件转换工具为例，说明LLM如何简化开发流程。
• B0a04gl强调了LLM工具在捕捉用户产品思维和决策过程方面的潜力，认为如果能够记录和回放用户的操作和编辑理由，将形成宝贵的“应用决策记忆”，为产品开发提供长期价值。
• Asdev对Lovable的商业模式表示怀疑，认为其用户主要用于构建原型，项目完成度在60-70%后往往被放弃，导致高流失率。他质疑Lovable能否通过现有模式持续盈利。
• Logifail对“Lovable能构建所有其他软件”的说法表示怀疑，认为这种宣传过于夸张。
• Clvx指出Lovable等工具在可靠性和“Day 2操作”（即部署后的维护和扩展）上的不足，认为这些工具需要更好地整合生态系统以提高盈利能力。
• Jun8对Lovable的当前定价策略提出质疑，认为其可能过于便宜，旨在快速获取大量用户。他提到Lovable可以通过创建应用商店等手段增加收入。
• Nichochar分享了作为业内人士的观点，指出Lovable的用户流失率高且面临与其他服务（如Supabase）的合作问题，未来可能需要通过自建生态系统来解决问题。
• Maest对过度宣传Lovable的现象表示反感，认为相关内容往往言过其实。
• Exiguus认为Lovable在非技术用户中受欢迎，但对其能否满足专业开发需求持怀疑态度，认为其主要适合原型设计而非完整产品开发。
• Socketcluster介绍了自己的项目Saasufy，强调了专注于无服务器部分的策略，并指出AI公司正努力确保用户不绕过其聊天界面。
• Chaosprint对Lovable的订阅模式提出疑问，认为对于年轻公司而言，月度经常性收入（MRR）可能比年度经常性收入（ARR）更重要。
• Janalsncm分享了自己使用Lovable构建应用框架的经验，认为其在简单项目中表现出色，但在处理复杂项目时存在不足。
• Fokamul幽默地表示支持在企业环境中使用LLM工具，并预测网络安全将在2026年蓬勃发展。
• _Pdp_认为LLM工具目前主要用于创建简单应用，与之前的工具相比并无突破性进展，且软件开发的核心挑战在于维护而非编写新代码。

补充讨论：
• 关于Lovable的商业模式是否可持续存在争议，主要集中在用户流失率高和项目完成度低的问题。
• 多位评论者提到Lovable等工具在处理复杂项目和“Day 2操作”上的不足，认为需要加强生态系统整合和功能可靠性。
• 部分评论者对Lovable的过度宣传表示反感，认为其宣传内容往往言过其实。
• 一些评论者分享了作为业内人士的观点，指出Lovable在市场定位和商业策略上面临的挑战。

data.title: Ask HN: Anyone using augmented reality, VR, glasses, helmets etc. in industry?
data.author: NewUser76312
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AR/VR技术在各行业应用的现状、挑战与前景

不同观点：
• **AR技术在工业质量控制中的应用**：
   - isk517认为Hololens 2在质量控制(QC)中表现出色，能够提升工作效率和准确性。
   - 然而，他指出大公司对AR兴趣不足，Hololens 2硬件能力接近极限，技术尚未完全成熟。
   - 他还提到AR的核心价值是提升人工操作的效率，但科技公司更关注AI而非实用工具。

• **AR/VR设备在实际工作中的局限性**：
   - idkwhattocallme指出过去十年AR/VR设备存在重量、价格、易碎性、电池寿命短等问题。
   - 许多客户发现这些设备在实际操作中不如智能手机方便，主要用于查阅手册或通话。
   - 近期语音技术(LLMs)和Meta的“眼镜形态”设备重新引发了大公司的兴趣，正在探索新的应用场景如检查和表格填写。

• **VR设备在办公环境中的不适与健康风险**：
   - edent认为即使忽略费用和卫生问题，VR头戴设备仍会导致部分用户不适，且长时间佩戴不舒适、孤立感强。
   - 这些因素限制了VR在办公环境中的广泛应用。

• **AR技术在远程协助和培训中的成功案例**：
   - lormayna分享了在能源服务公司使用VR进行远程协助和培训的成功案例，显著节省了时间和成本。

• **消费级AR设备的使用体验**：
   - gavinray和j-wags分享了个人使用Viture Pro XR和TCL Rayneo Air 2显示眼镜的体验，指出了设备设计和舒适度方面的问题。
   - 他们期待未来AR设备的改进和更多市场选择。

• **AR/VR在工程和建筑行业中的应用挑战**：
   - ugolino91提到AR/VR平台在工程和建筑行业中仍面临硬件限制，不能完全替代传统PC工作流。
   - 这些设备只能在特定场景下使用，尚需与2D显示器配合。

• **特定场景下的AR需求与设备限制**：
   - wiseleo指出在复杂工作场景（如高空作业）中，AR技术有实际需求，但目前设备尚未普及。
   - spookie提到AR设备在特殊职业培训（如消防员）中面临电池寿命和耐用性的挑战。

补充讨论：
• **企业对AR/VR设备的接受度与投资回报**：
   - SomeUserName432提到Equinor（挪威石油公司）使用Hololens的成功案例。
   - curiouscavalier指出AR/VR在培训中的应用比公众认知的要广泛，但在实际操作中面临设备可靠性和工作流程改变的阻力。
   - 企业对AR/VR的ROI（投资回报）和设备适应性仍持观望态度，许多决策者缺乏实际使用经验。

• **远程工作与便携式虚拟桌面环境的探索**：
   - geocrasher提到正在考虑使用Oculus 3作为便携式虚拟桌面环境，以替代大型显示器，适应远程工作需求。

• **AR/VR在CAD数据可视化中的潜力与挑战**：
   - jlarocco指出其公司在CAD数据翻译工具中尝试支持VR眼镜，但后续进展不大，主要挑战在于是否能为客户带来足够的价值。

争议焦点：
• **AR/VR设备是否能在实际工作中广泛应用**：
   - 一方面，支持者认为AR/VR在特定行业和场景中能显著提升效率和降低成本。
   - 另一方面，批评者指出设备的技术限制、使用不便和市场接受度低等问题，认为科技公司应更关注实用性而非创新噱头。

本文讲述了一次调试过程，涉及Bash、OverlayFS以及一个30年前的意外问题。最初，客户报告在切换到OverlayFS后，OpenSSH的scp命令失败，错误信息显示为"shell-init: error retrieving current directory: getcwd: cannot access parent directories: Inappropriate ioctl for device"。经过分析，发现问题出在Bash自己的getcwd()实现上，而非glibc或内核问题。

调查发现，Bash在编译时由于交叉编译环境问题，错误地认为系统的getcwd()不可用，从而使用了内部的备用实现。这个备用实现是为缺乏现代功能的旧系统设计的，不适用于OverlayFS。具体来说，OverlayFS在处理目录inode时与Bash的旧算法不兼容，导致错误。

最终，通过参考Yocto项目的做法，明确配置bash_cv_getcwd_malloc解决此问题。修复后，错误消失，问题得到解决。

主要讨论点：POSIX API中errno和相关函数的复杂性及其导致的长期未被发现的bug，以及跨平台配置工具（如autoconf）的问题。

不同观点：
• **chubot**：认为POSIX API在处理errno时令人沮丧，通常不需要手动设置errno，但在某些情况下（如readdir()）则需要。他还提到在开发Oils项目时发现并修复了一个与$PWD相关的bug，这个问题在AT&T ksh中存在了30多年。他还指出shell不能单纯依赖getcwd()，需要结合继承的$PWD和当前值来判断路径。

• **JonChesterfield**：对bug报告的回应感到失望。修复方法是设置errno=0以确保错误信息合理，但回应中却有人以“文件系统不应这样工作”为由提出反对意见。

• **jwilk**：提供了相关的bug报告链接，但没有深入讨论技术细节。

• **justincormack**：认为configure脚本中的检查大多已经过时，尤其在跨平台编译时容易出问题。很多系统已经禁用了一些老旧的检查，比如Nix在2017年所做的更改。

• **saurik**：指出在交叉编译时，忽略警告并依赖默认设置是不可取的。开发者应该更仔细地处理配置问题，要么手动提供autoconf所需的信息，要么确保能在目标系统上运行二进制文件。

• **malkia**：认为autoconf虽然表面上看起来容易使用，但实际会以难以理清的方式出错。他更倾向于针对特定平台进行有限配置，以确保编译时明确知道哪些定义可用，而不是猜测主机环境。

• **pogopop77**：认为这是一个有趣的调查，展示了新的文件系统范式（如overlay filesystems）如何微妙地影响行为，导致难以追踪的复杂问题。

• **akoboldfrying**：以幽默方式指出，软件开发中需要考虑的不仅是某个条件是否满足，还要考虑各种其他因素（如特定操作系统问题），暗示开发的复杂性。

• **x0x0**：认为这个问题说明了软件开发的困难。长期以来，readdir()的inode号码有特定语义，但支持overlay文件系统需要改变这些语义，而大量软件是基于旧语义开发的，导致升级困难。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于POSIX API设计是否合理，尤其是在errno处理和readdir()函数的行为上。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是autoconf等跨平台配置工具在现代开发环境中的局限性和问题。
- 评论中多次提到历史遗留问题，如30多年未修复的bug，反映出软件维护的长尾效应。

Deep Down the Rabbit Hole: Bash, OverlayFS, and a 30-Year-Old Surprise
This blog post recounts a recent debugging session that uncovered a surprising set of issues involving Bash,
getcwd()
1
, and OverlayFS
2
.
What began as a simple customer bug report evolved into a deep dive worth sharing.
Initial Bug Report
A customer reported that OpenSSH scp
3
failed after switching to OverlayFS.
We found the following error in the logs:
shell-init: error retrieving current directory: \
getcwd: cannot access parent directories: Inappropriate ioctl for device
After analyzing the report, we realized the message didn’t come from scp itself but from the Bash shell.
We asked the key question: why couldn’t Bash determine the current working directory, and why did it fail with
ENOTTY
(Inappropriate ioctl for device)?
Ruling Out the Kernel
Because the issue appeared after the introduction of OverlayFS, we reviewed the OverlayFS source code in the Linux kernel for any code paths that return
ENOTTY
.
Although such paths exist, we considered hitting them highly unlikely.
Bash uses glibc and is written in C.
We examined the glibc system call wrapper for
getcwd()
but found no logic that could return
ENOTTY
.
The wrapper mainly handles buffer allocation and falls back to a generic implementation if the system call fails.
To test this theory, we enabled system call tracing.
Surprisingly, the trace revealed that the
getcwd()
system call never got called.
Since glibc offers multiple
getcwd()
implementations depending on the system, we double-checked that we had reviewed the correct Linux-specific one.
We found no code path that bypassed the system call.
Bash’s home made
getcwd()
A hunch led us to check how Bash links to the
getcwd
symbol:
$ nm -D bash | grep getcwd
...
000c7b10 T getcwd
...
This showed that Bash includes its own
getcwd()
function rather than relying on glibc’s version.
We expected this output instead:
$ nm -D bash | grep getcwd
...
U getcwd
...
Surprised, we inspected the Bash source and confirmed it does contain a
getcwd()
implementation, but guarded by the following:
#if !defined (HAVE_GETCWD)
Developers originally intended this fallback for ancient Unix systems lacking the
getcwd()
system call.
On Linux,
HAVE_GETCWD
should normally be defined.
We confirmed in
config.h
:
#define HAVE_GETCWD 1
At first, this puzzled us because under normal conditions, the implementation should never compile.
But further inspection of
config-bot.h
showed this logic:
#if defined (HAVE_GETCWD) && defined (GETCWD_BROKEN) && !defined (SOLARIS)
#  undef HAVE_GETCWD
#endif
Sure enough, our
config.h
defined
GETCWD_BROKEN
.
That explained why Bash used its internal fallback.
But why did the system consider
getcwd()
broken?
Cross-Compilation Confusion
We examined the output of the
configure
script in detail to trace the origin of
GETCWD_BROKEN
.
We found this line:
checking if getcwd() will dynamically allocate memory with 0 size... \
configure: WARNING: cannot check whether getcwd allocates memory when cross-compiling \
-- defaulting to no
The check in
aclocal.m4
sets
GETCWD_BROKEN
if it can’t confirm that
getcwd()
allocates memory with a zero-size buffer.
Since the build occurred in a cross-compilation environment, the test defaulted to failure.
We discovered that Bash becomes problematic in cross-compilation environments.
Since Bash is cross-compiled for ARM in this specific setup, this made sense.
We then wondered why this issue wasn’t more widespread.
After all, both Bash and OverlayFS are common in embedded systems.
Next, we looked into how major embedded Linux projects like Yocto handle cross-compiling Bash.
Although the Bash Yocto recipe didn’t mention
getcwd
, we found this line in
meta/site/common-glibc
:
bash_cv_getcwd_malloc
=
${
bash_cv_getcwd_malloc
=yes
}
Yocto explicitly overrides the test result to avoid the fallback.
The embedded Linux build system we used didn’t apply such a workaround.
This clarified the issue.
After we implemented a similar override, the issue vanished.
Root Cause Analysis
At this point, we had identified and fixed the bug.
But several questions remained:
Why did the issue appear only with OverlayFS?
Why did Bash’s fallback
getcwd()
fail?
During testing, we observed another error message:
shell-init: error retrieving current directory: \
getcwd: cannot access parent directories: Success
This indicated that
errno
was sometimes set to
0
, suggesting no error occurred, yet
getcwd()
still failed.
OverlayFS and Inode Numbers
To answer the remaining questions, we analyzed Bash’s
getcwd()
implementation.
On Linux, you can determine the current working directory in two ways:
Use the
getcwd()
system call
Read the
/proc/self/cwd
symlink
Bash’s implementation used neither, aiming to support systems lacking these features.
In fact, the fallback dates back to the last millennium.
It used a classic Unix algorithm to reconstruct the working directory path:

data.title: How to Write Compelling Release Announcements
data.author: mtlynch
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了如何改进发布公告的撰写，使其更关注用户体验而非技术细节。文章指出，许多发布公告仅简单罗列新功能，像 changelog 一样，缺乏对用户实际使用场景的描述。好的发布公告应强调新功能对用户的实际好处，使用户感到兴奋。例如，不要只说添加了“重复”按钮，而要说明用户可以用此按钮创建定期事件，简化操作。发布公告应突出对用户体验影响最大的变化，而非技术实现细节。此外，公告还应简要介绍产品，吸引新用户，同时不忽视现有用户。最后，避免使用“各种改进和错误修复”这样模糊的表述。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何撰写发布公告和发布说明，特别是在内容详尽程度、营销语气和用户关注点之间的平衡。

不同观点：
• **支持详尽的发布说明**：
  - lapcat认为发布说明应尽量详尽，包括所有修复的bug和新引入的问题，以便用户了解软件的变化。
  - 作为独立开发者，lapcat的用户对详尽的发布说明表示赞赏。
  - 反对将发布说明用于营销目的，认为这是对用户的烦扰。

• **支持简明、用户导向的发布公告**：
  - deanebarker和loughnane支持简明扼要的发布公告，强调直接说明实际变化，而非包装成营销信息。
  - loughnane建议通过减少文字来避免读者失去兴趣，例如“Create events 10x faster”的示例。

• **平衡详尽与简明**：
  - deanebarker建议可以有两套说明：一套简明的基础说明，另一套较为详细的“润色”说明。
  - ednite认为发布公告应结合用户体验透明地说明修复和改进，同时建议维护一份详细的技术 changelog 以供内部参考。

• **关注营销与用户价值**：
  - ukuina和chapz批评过度营销化的发布公告，认为这忽视了实际的用户需求。
  - flpm和thewisenerd则认为发布公告应强调对用户的价值，并通过选择性 spotlight 最重要的改进以吸引用户注意。

• **关于具体示例和数值描述的争议**：
  - awkward提醒对具体数值应谨慎使用，以免误导不成熟的用户或被成熟用户识破夸大。
  - jcalx强调写作应根据用户实际需求和痛点进行，避免不必要的技术细节和数字描述。

补充讨论：
• **发布公告的读者对象**：
  - simonw指出发布公告不仅是给现有用户看的，也可能是新用户的第一次接触点，因此需要兼顾不同读者的需求。

• **标题的重要性**：
  - continuational强调发布公告的标题应传达新版本的核心和有趣之处，而非简单的版本号。

• **对营销化发布的反感**：
  - temodox明确表示不喜欢营销化的发布公告，认为纯技术性的发布说明已经足够。

争议焦点：如何在发布公告中平衡详尽的技术细节和简明的用户价值描述，以及是否应将发布说明用于营销目的。

44377666.article_content:
A release announcement showcases how the user’s experience is better today than it was yesterday. That sounds obvious, but most release announcements seem to forget that there’s a user at all.
So many release announcements just enumerate new features in a way that’s totallly divorced from how real people use the software. The announcement is essentially just a changelog with better writing.
For example, here’s a “changelog” style of announcing a new feature:
Bad: Describe what the dev team did rather than how it benefits the user
Added “repeat” button to the event menu.
Don’t just tell the user that there’s a new button. Tell the user what they can do with that button.
Good: Describe how changes benefit the user
Create recurring events automatically
🔗
In previous versions, the only way you could create weekly, monthly, or any type of recurring event was to duplicate events manually for every occurence. Duplicating events this way was tedious and error-prone.
Our latest release allows you to create recurring events automatically. Click “Options > Repeat”, and you’ll find flexible settings for repeating events on any schedule you want. You can even sync with your company’s holiday schedule to automatically skip event dates that fall on a company holiday.
Note that the example doesn’t boast about what the software can do. It tells the user what they can do with the software. It speaks directly to the user, describing what happens when “you” create events.
Release notes are not release announcements
🔗
Some software companies dump their commit history into a document, add some headings, and call that a release announcement.
Not a release announcement
That is not a release announcement. Those are release
notes
.
Release notes are fine and practical, but they’re boring.
You can publish release notes as well, but if you want users to feel excited about your newest release, give them something more interesting to read than a sterile changelog.
What to feature in a release announcement
🔗
A release announcement is a summary of the changes that will have the greatest impact on the user’s experience. It presents them in a clear, accessible way that focuses on the user.
In contrast to release notes, which aim to be exhaustive, release announcements include only the most impactful changes.
To decide which features to include in the release announcement, consider these questions:
What can the user do in the latest version that they couldn’t before?
Which workflows became easier?
Which workflows became faster?
Notice that the questions don’t include, “Which feature took the longest to complete” or “What feature contains the cleverest algorithm?”
I’ve published releases where the flagship feature was a performance improvement that only took a few hours of dev work. Implementation cost doesn’t always correlate with end-user value.
Call it “faster” not “less slow”
🔗
Some bugs are so frustrating and time-consuming to fix that you forget why you’re even fixing them in the first place. You lose sight of how the bug affects the user’s experience.
Bad: Focus on what was previously broken
Fixed a thread deadlock that froze the UI for up to two second when creating a new file.
From the user’s perspective, the new version isn’t just the same software minus a bug — it’s a tangibly better experience.
Focus on the improvement rather than the flaw. Instead of declaring the absence of a bug, celebrate how you improved the user’s experience:
Good: Focus on the improvement rather than the previous flaw
We sped up new file creation, so you can now create a new file in under 20ms, a 100x speedup from v1.2.
Briefly introduce your product
🔗
In addition to building loyalty with existing users, a release announcement should pique the interest of new, potential users.
If you publish your release announcement to the web, many of the people who read it will have never heard of your product at all.
Bad: Take it for granted that readers know your product
I’m excited to announce the 1.0 release of OpenVQ9! After 17 years of hard work, this release is a triumph for all OpenVQ9 fans, as well as the loyal developers in the OpenVQ9 ecosystem (all of whom know what OpenVQ9 is, so there’s no need to explain it here).
Early in your announcement, include a quick explanation of what your product does. If the reader isn’t familiar with your product, what’s the least they need to know to understand the rest of your announcement?
Good: Succinctly explain your product for readers unfamiliar with it
I’m excited to announce the 1.0 release of OpenVQ9, the fully open and customizable software for robot vaccum cleaners.
Don’t alienate your existing users with a 20-paragraph introduction to a product they already know. A sentence or two will provide context for new users without diluting your announcement with excessive noise for existing users.
No more “various improvements and bugfixes”
🔗
A release announcement should never include the phrase, “various improvements and

  - simonw指出发布公告不仅是给现有用户看的，也可能是新用户的第一次接触点，因此需要兼顾不同读者的需求。

• **标题的重要性**：
  - continuational强调发布公告的标题应传达新版本的核心和有趣之处，而非简单的版本号。

• **对营销化发布的反感**：
  - temodox明确表示不喜欢营销化的发布公告，认为纯技术性的发布说明已经足够。

争议焦点：如何在发布公告中平衡详尽的技术细节和简明的用户价值描述，以及是否应将发布说明用于营销目的。

**PEP 723** 提出了一种在单文件 Python 脚本中嵌入元数据的方法，帮助启动器和 IDE 等工具处理脚本。通过结合 **uv** 和 **PEP 723**，可以轻松运行带有依赖的 Python 脚本。文章还展示了一个提取 YouTube 视频字幕的示例脚本，通过在脚本中加入 shebang 行和元数据，使其可以直接作为可执行文件运行。这种方法使 Python 脚本的执行更加便捷，类似于 Go 语言的自包含二进制文件。

不同观点：
• ACAVJW4H认为Python脚本现在可以更轻松地运行，但Shell脚本的依赖管理和可复现性依然落后，仍依赖于手动步骤或不安全的`curl | bash`方法。虽然有Nix和Docker等工具，但它们要么复杂，要么不实用。

Fun with uv and PEP 723
June 24, 2025
For the longest time, I have been frustrated with Python because I couldnât use it for one-off scripts. I had to first ensure it was running in an environment where it could find the right Python version and the dependencies installed. That is now a thing of the past.
uv
Â¶
If you are not a Pythonista (or one possibly living under a rock),
uv
is
an extremely fast Python package and project manager, written in Rust.
uv also provides this nifty tool called
uvx
(kinda like
npx
from the Node/NPM ecosystem for Javascript/Typescript packages) which can be used to invoke a Python tool inside a package.
uvx
takes care of creating a (cached) disposable virtual environment, setting up the right Python version and installing all the dependencies before running.
For example
$ uvx ruff --version
Installed 1 package in 5ms
ruff 0.12.0
PEP 723 - Inline script metadata
Â¶
PEP 723
is a Python Enhancement Proposal that
specifies a metadata format that can be embedded in single-file Python scripts to assist launchers, IDEs and other external tools which may need to interact with such scripts.
Here is the example directly lifted from the proposal:
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "requests<3",
#   "rich",
# ]
# ///
import
requests
from
rich.pretty
import
pprint
resp
=
requests.get(
"https://peps.python.org/api/peps.json"
)
data
=
resp.json()
pprint([(k, v[
"title"
])
for
k, v
in
data.items()][:
10
])
Using uv and PEP 723 metadata to run a Python script
Â¶
Combining uv and the PEP-723 metadata inside a Python script, we can run the script in the previous section as follows:
$ uv run pep.py
Installed 9 packages in 24ms
[
â   ('1', 'PEP Purpose and Guidelines'),
â   ('2', 'Procedure for Adding New Modules'),
â   ('3', 'Guidelines for Handling Bug Reports'),
â   ('4', 'Deprecation of Standard Modules'),
â   ('5', 'Guidelines for Language Evolution'),
â   ('6', 'Bug Fix Releases'),
â   ('7', 'Style Guide for C Code'),
â   ('8', 'Style Guide for Python Code'),
â   ('9', 'Sample Plaintext PEP Template'),
â   ('10', 'Voting Guidelines')
]
A more useful example - extracting YouTube transcripts from an executable Python script
Â¶
We can combine things we covered in the previous sections to create a simple executable script that can extract YouTube transcripts.
First we create a Python script with a shebang and inline metadata.
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.8"
# dependencies = [
#     "youtube-transcript-api",
# ]
# ///
import
sys
import
re
from
youtube_transcript_api
import
YouTubeTranscriptApi
from
youtube_transcript_api.formatters
import
TextFormatter
if
len
(sys.argv)
<
2
:
print
(
'Usage: provide YouTube URL or video_id as argument'
,
file
=
sys.stderr)
sys.exit(
1
)
url_or_id
=
sys.argv[
1
]
# Extract video ID from URL if it's a full URL
video_id_match
=
re.search(
r
'
(?:
v=
|
/
)([a-zA-Z0-9_-]
{11}
)
'
, url_or_id)
if
video_id_match:
video_id
=
video_id_match.group(
1
)
else
:
# Assume it's already a video ID
video_id
=
url_or_id
try
:
ytt_api
=
YouTubeTranscriptApi()
transcript
=
ytt_api.fetch(video_id)
formatter
=
TextFormatter()
print
(formatter.format_transcript(transcript))
except
Exception
as
e:
print
(
f
'Error:
{
e
}
'
,
file
=
sys.stderr)
sys.exit(
1
)
Note the shebang line:
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
. It is important to specify
uv run
with the
--script
flag when used on the shebang line.
We save this script as
ytt
and then make it executable with
chmod +x ytt
.
We can now run the script like:
$ ./ytt https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zgSQr0d5EVg
Installed 7 packages in 10ms
hey it's Matt here and today I'm going
to show you how to use UV not only to
install packages in your python projects
but to manage entire projects to create
virtual environments and even how to
manage entire versions of python with UV
uh and hopefully you'll understand by
any of this video UV is a dropin
â¦<snipped text>â¦
Fun times
Â¶
This opens up a lot of possibilities for running Python code more seamlessly. Before this I used to prefer
Go
for one-off scripts because it was easy to create a self-contained binary executable. But now that I could use uv, I coded up a quick MCP server in Python for extracting YouTube transcripts. Check it out on Github at
cottongeeks/ytt-mcp
.
More resources
Â¶
Running scripts | uv
Tools | uv
Using uv as an installer | aider

All Articles
Some thoughts on my first YC Demo Day
23 June 2025
#investing
#yc
This year was my first time attending YC Demo Day.
It’s a fascinating event and, really a fascinating product for investors.
Growing up in the bay area, I remember over a decade ago admiring people in YC. I was always impressed and it is a real privilege to be able to attend from the other side (as an investor).
I went not because I am a prolific investor, I went because I thought that it would be a unique experience.
The Product: Startups
This seems obvious, but the startups are the product, demo day is not a celebration of their achievement over the course of the batch, IMO it’s much more of an assembly line.
To be honest, it’s a variation
this woman on Douyin
, but applied to startups.
This woman shows a product for 3 seconds before moving onto the next one.
Rinse and repeat.
That’s YC demo day.
1 slide.
1 minute pitches.
1 speaker.
Startups are marched up there.
They get their one minute of fame and then walk off. That’s it.
All the startups are clearly coached, they communicate similarly (hand gestures, etc), every slide format is the roughly the same down to the number of bullet points.
They all conform to a particular mold.
1
The Buyer: Investors
As an investor you get access to a little website where you can view the videos. You can also get intro’d to the startup via email or message them directly.
You setup your profile in there and so you’ve got to appear legitimate as well.
what you get
The program heavily filters these batches for high-agency people and folks who want to get after it.
The program has already vetted these people as those willing to sacrifice and make things happen, including dropouts leaving successful jobs. It’s an admirable collection of people.
The base terms for investments
2 on 20 is the standard for startups coming out of YC. It seems to me that this is the benchmark for what the teams are going for and you can get a sense for excitement based on how filled out that allocation is.
Notable Themes
Vertical AI was all over the place.
Cursor for X was also prevalent.
This is more of a reflection on the event itself, so I won’t go into too much detail but it’s an interesting pulse of not only what people want to build but also what people want to invest in.
The community
I met some pretty amazing folks. Exited founders, internet friends. It’s a pretty astonishing collection and community and there’s quite a bit of value there.
It honestly felt a bit more like a business festival, the networking was bumping and there’s real momentum there. I met a lot of interesting people, people that I wouldn’t have gotten exposure to otherwise.
Conclusions
It was a great event. I enjoyed it, if you have the opportunity, I’d recommend going. It’s a spectacle!
Footnotes
Note, I don’t mean this negatively. It’s just they’ve got a format that works, that is the standard, and you’ve got to deliver against that.

data.title: A lumberjack created more than 200 sculptures in Wisconsin's Northwoods
data.author: noleary
data.article_summary: 退休伐木工弗雷德·史密斯在20世纪40年代末至60年代中期，于威斯康星州创建了超过200座真人大小的混凝土雕塑，这些雕塑展现了当地文化、民间传说以及美国历史和爱国主义象征。史密斯的作品核心为木结构，外包水泥、镶嵌碎玻璃等物品，如今保存在威斯康星混凝土公园。由于长期暴露于自然环境中，雕塑需要持续维护，保护员使用环氧树脂、硅胶等材料修复破损和不稳，并加固生锈的支撑结构。公园免费开放，但鼓励捐款以支持保护工作。

44393160.article_content:
Over the years, a conservator replaced the headgear on deer with real antlers and the originals mounted on moose with synthetic alternatives.
Carol M. Highsmith/Buyenlarge/Getty Images
During Fred Smith’s golden years, art inexplicably began to pour out of him. The retired lumberjack loved to work with his hands, think with his hands, speak with his hands—and one day, like magic, he began to create with his hands.
Bent over by age and arthritis, the Phillips, Wisconsin, resident continued to build life-size and larger-than-life concrete sculptures—over 200 in all—from the late 1940s to the mid-1960s, blending local culture and lore with the wider world and the great beyond.
Smith’s homestead farm soon filled with images from his life and imagination as he depicted everything from everyday folks to folk heroes, as well as symbols of American history, patriotism and spirituality.
The sculptures are loosely organized by theme. Even so, the panorama of animals, humans and objects all seem to mix and mingle in the same landscape, leading to plenty of intriguing juxtapositions. Picture everything from Sacagawea and the Statue of Liberty to a
musky
so massive it’s pulled by a team of horses.
When asked about his monuments, Smith, who died in 1976 at 89 years old, would simply respond with laughter. “Nobody knows why I made them,”
he said
. “Not even me.”
Retired lumberjack Fred Smith built more than 200 sculptures on his farm from the late 1940s to the mid-1960s.
Wisconsin Concrete Park
Unable to read or write, he taught himself to form these sculptures using wooden structures at their core wrapped in mink or barbed wire, covered in layers of cement, and adorned with broken glass and other found objects.
Today, his eclectic display lives on at the
Wisconsin Concrete Park
, an outdoor sculpture garden situated within a
16-acre setting
in the state’s sparsely populated Northwoods region, where the trees outnumber the people.
What shines through in Smith’s work—nearly half a century after his departure—is a profound reverence for nature and for the many ordinary and extraordinary people, places and events explored throughout his art.
Preservation tools and techniques
Surviving the area’s elements, particularly the long and frigid winters, is easier said than done, though. What visitors may overlook is the painstaking upkeep that goes into these folk art statues that are exposed to Mother Nature’s whims and Father Time’s unrelenting wear and tear.
This past year, for example, a tree branch took Paul Bunyan’s head off, injured his arm and walloped one of his wolfhounds in one fell swoop, says Ann Grzywnowicz, operations manager of the
Friends of Fred Smith
, a nonprofit formed to preserve the park and develop it into an educational and cultural facility.
Restoring the legendary lumberjack to his former glory will be one of the biggest and most significant projects awaiting Ben Caguioa, a sculpture conservator based in Chicago, when he returns this summer to tackle the most recent round of destruction caused by wind, water and winter.
Need to know: How to visit the Wisconsin Concrete Park
The Wisconsin Concrete Park is located just south of Phillips, in Price County, Wisconsin.
The park is open to the public year-round during daylight hours. No admission is required, but donations are encouraged, as the funds go toward preservation work.
His toolbox includes a range of materials—such as marine epoxies, fumed silica and elastomeric caulking—meant to restore structural integrity and aesthetic appeal. This undertaking involves repairing breaks, fixing instabilities, strengthening sculptures or leveling those that have begun to tilt.
Along the way, Caguioa has replaced antlers, reinforced legs and re-leveled the big fish. He has also worked extensively on the lumberjacks near the park entrance, one of which completely collapsed and had to be rebuilt from the ground up.
Many of these sculptures were assembled around wooden two-by-fours, and these box frames—especially within the human figures—gradually decay. The armature that runs up through the legs is made of galvanized pipe that rusts out.
Since there are only two points of contact with the ground, the statues eventually begin to wobble. To reinforce ankles, Caguioa inserts stainless steel rods within the galvanized pipe or replaces that pipe with a steel rod of equivalent thickness.
On breaks and cracks, the conservator uses marine epoxies to establish a solid connection. “I’ll inject that into the cracks using a syringe,” Caguioa says. When he needs to fill a larger gap, he thickens the epoxy with fumed silica to achieve a consistency that resembles a viscous ointment. From there, Caguioa disguises the fractures using elastomeric caulking dusted with sand to replicate the appearance of the original concrete.
If the sculpture spans two or more bases or if the original base is cracked, he’ll use flexible joints to compensate for the movement, much like the
expansion join

data.title: Ask HN: Is anyone else just done with the industry?
data.author: MongooseStudios
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件开发行业的职业倦怠、行业变化以及应对策略

不同观点：
• [tptacek] 认为每隔7-8年就会产生一次职业倦怠，并指出在这种情绪下做出的决定往往是不理智的。他以自身经验说明这种感觉是周期性的，建议不要在此时做出重大决定。

• [_wire_] 对企业持批判态度，认为企业并不是人道机构，而是以利益为重，不惜牺牲有技能和责任感的员工。他还指出，所谓的智能和进步只是特权阶层的夸张说法，当公司福利枯竭时，这个阶层也会随之消亡。

• [tonestonestones] 认为软件开发正走向自动化，这是不可避免的自然演变。虽然不幸，但也是一种机会，可以去做更有趣的事情。他还提到管理者需要被替换，除非他们能比技术人员看得更远。

• [protocolture] 表达了对当前工作环境的不满，指出雇主和客户都在维持过时的做法，而不愿投资于技术更新，这让他们付出了更高的成本。

• [m0llusk] 认为软件工程师有能力创建自己的公司，不必局限于行业内的工作，这可能是摆脱当前困境的一种途径。

• [AdamH12113] 建议离开硅谷，去小公司工作，这些公司虽然无法提供高薪，但工作可能更有意义，能带来不同的满足感。

• [colechristensen] 认为倦怠和负面情绪是可以理解的，但建议寻求专业帮助，通过积极的方式来处理这些情绪，找到新的方向，而不是让愤怒伤害自己。

• [jaronilan] 分享了一篇幽默文章，暗示当前招聘市场的困境，间接支持了对行业现状的批评。

• [itsthecourier] 指出LLMs（大型语言模型）的应用将大大减少对人力的需求，尤其是对高级工程师的需求，这给行业带来了更大压力，并提到自2021年以来行业的收缩。

• [gedy] 提醒大家当前是市场低谷，公司会变得非常挑剔，自学成才的人在此时可能不占优势。他还指出，软件行业过去几十年过得很轻松，其他行业的情况可能更糟。

• [regflid] 对某些评论中的傲慢和性别歧视态度提出批评，指出这种态度可能是导致个人职业困境的原因之一。

• [crsv] 持强硬态度，认为世界本就是残酷的，个人不应期待被给予任何东西，而应自强不息。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是对企业和管理者的不满情绪，一些人如[_wire_]和[protocolture]对企业持强烈批判态度，而[regflid]则认为这种批判可能是个人问题导致的。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是LLMs和自动化对行业的冲击，[tonestonestones]和[itsthecourier]都提到了自动化对就业市场的负面影响。
• 职业倦怠和应对策略也是一个重要讨论点，[colechristensen]建议通过积极的方式处理情绪，而[AdamH12113]则提出通过地理位置的改变来寻找新的机会。

data.title: Collections: Nitpicking Gladiator's Iconic Opening Battle, Part I
data.author: diodorus
data.article_summary: 文章分析了电影《角斗士》(2000)开场战斗场景的历史准确性，指出该场景尽管视觉上看似真实，实际上充满了历史错误。文章提到，虽然这场战斗场景在公众想象中塑造了对罗马军队的认知，但其细节如军队组成、战术、武器和胜利策略等均不符历史事实。特别指出，场景中罗马军队过于依赖骑兵和弓箭手，而这并不符合当时罗马军队的战斗方式。此外，文章还以主角“Maximus Decimus Meridius”的名字为例，说明其看似像罗马名字，实则完全不符罗马命名 conventions。文章强调，该场景营造了一种“貌似真实”的效果，但并非真正的历史再现，提醒观众不应被表面的视觉细节所误导。文章作者表明，尽管《角斗士》在历史细节上有诸多错误，但仍可以欣赏这部电影，只需认识到其历史不准确性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电影《罗马》的历史准确性与艺术创作自由之间的平衡

不同观点：
• **Shorel**：认为导演有权追求电影艺术表现，但历史学家也有权指出与历史不符之处。历史科学的传播与电影本身同样重要，电影不应只追求商业利益，准确呈现历史事件同样重要。
• **ChrisMarshallNY**：关注细节错误，例如罗马士兵使用马镫的问题，指出这些小细节可能对历史真实性有重大影响。
• **robin_reala**：对电影取景地选择提出质疑，认为 Bourne Woods 的场景让观众难以进入电影设定的德国地域背景，影响观影体验。
• **Notatheist**：认为仅仅指出错误并不足够，建议应提供合理的解决方案或解释导演可能做出这些决定的原因，特别是考虑到历史准确性可能带来的高成本问题。
• **Hizonner**：对电影的叙事和表演提出严厉批评，认为电影不仅历史不准确，且剧情幼稚、表演生硬，整体观感极其无聊。
• **ggm**：理解并支持导演 Ridley Scott 的创作选择，认为他关注视觉美感和一定的历史“可接受性”，但并不拘泥于所有细节。同时指出 Scott 对被挑剔历史错误感到不满。
• **Rebelgecko**：指出电影中的服装错误，特别是战斗后有人穿着牛仔裤，严重影响历史氛围。
• **staplung**：提到电视剧《罗马》第一季第一集中的战斗场景，认为可以作为比较，尽管预算较低。
• **dmurray**：认为大多数批评属于挑剔细节，指出罗马军队在艺术作品中通常被描绘得更统一，且不同历史时期的混用属于艺术创作自由。同时，认为与现代武器出现在历史战役中的类比不恰当。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于历史准确性与艺术创作自由的平衡。部分评论者如 Shorel 和 ggm 认为历史准确性至关重要，而 Notatheist 和 dmurray 则强调艺术创作的自由和现实拍摄的限制。
• 评论中还涉及到电影的具体细节错误，如服装和取景地选择，这些细节影响了观众的沉浸体验。
• 总体上，讨论反映了观众和专业人士对历史题材电影的不同期待，以及对导演创作意图的理解和批评。

This week, we’re going to take a close look at arguably the most famous and recognizable Roman battle sequence in film: the iconic opening battle from
Gladiator

The iconic opening battle, set in the Marcomannic Wars (166-180) during the reign of Marcus Aurelius (r. 161-180)
dominates
the pop-cultural reference points for the Roman army in battle and you can see its heavy influence in things like how the
Total War
series presents Roman armies (particularly in trailers and other promotional material).  Students and enthusiasts alike will often cite this sequence as the thing which sparked their interest in the Roman army.  It is hard to overstate how
pervasive
its influence is in the public imagination of what the Roman army, particularly of the imperial period, was like, especially as its style is imitated by later pop culture works.
Which is why it is so unfortunate that it is such a deceptive historical mess
. This sequence
in particular
is a banner example of what I’ve termed elsewhere the ‘
perils of historical verisimilitude
,’ the habit of historically based popular-culture works including what we might think of as fake
signifiers
of research, things that
seem
historically grounded rather than
being
historically grounded, as a way to cheaply cash in on the cachet that an actually grounded representation gets a work.
Gladiator
actually provides a perfect metaphor for this: its main character’s name.  Russell Crowe proudly informs us he is, “Maximus Decimus Meridius,” a name that certainly
sounds
suitably Roman, picking up the three-part name with that standard second declension -us ending.  It
sounds
like it could be a real name – if you didn’t know Latin you would probably
assume
that it could be a real Roman name.  But,
as we’ve noted
,
it isn’t a Roman name
and in fact
gets nearly all of the Roman naming conventions wrong
: Roman names are ordered as praenomen, nomen and cognomen, with the nomen indicating one’s
gens
(‘clan’ more or less) and the praenomen selected from just a couple dozen common personal names.  Decimus is one of those two-dozen common praenomina (which also means it is never going to show up as the name of a
gens
), so it ought to go first as it is actually his personal name.  Meanwhile Maximus (‘the greatest’) is very much
not
one of those roughly two-dozen praenomina, instead being always cognomen (essentially a nickname).  Finally Meridius isn’t a Latin word at all (so it can’t be a praenomen personal name nor a cognomen nickname),

Every part of his name is wrong
and it
should

sounds just right enough

being entirely wrong

like
truth), rather than veristic (realistic, true).

visual

only

.  The
visual

check

data.title: Apple Research unearthed forgotten AI technique and using it to generate images
data.author: celias
data.article_summary:
苹果公司通过两篇新论文重新挖掘了一种被遗忘的AI技术——归一化流（Normalizing Flows），并用于图像生成。与目前主流的扩散模型和自回归模型不同，归一化流模型通过学习将真实数据转换为结构化噪声并反向生成新样本。其优势在于能精确计算生成图像的概率，适用于对结果概率要求高的任务。

第一篇论文介绍的TarFlow模型引入了Transformer块，将图像分割成小块进行自回归生成，避免了图像压缩成固定词汇导致的质量损失。第二篇论文的STARFlow模型进一步改进，在压缩后的潜在空间中生成图像，再通过解码器恢复到高分辨率，提升了生成效率和图像质量。

与OpenAI的GPT-4o通过序列化标记生成图像不同，苹果的模型直接生成像素值，更适合移动设备，展现了其在便携设备上的潜力。
